questions.def: Use 'have to' to express obligation.
questions.question: You ___ to be on time for the meeting.

questions.def: 'Should' is used to give advice.
questions.question: He ___ see a doctor. He feels terrible.

questions.def: After 'must' we use the base form of the verb (without 'to').
questions.question: She must to finish the report today.

questions.def: 'Advise' is the verb form, used to give recommendations.
questions.question: I ___ you to take a break.

questions.def: 'Shouldn't' is used to give negative advice.
questions.question: You ___ eat so much sugar.

questions.def: Use 'have to' to express obligation.
questions.question: We ___ to wear a uniform at school.

questions.def: 'Obliged' is the past participle, used with 'are'.
questions.question: Are we ___ to buy tickets?

questions.def: 'Have to' expresses necessity.
questions.question: I ___ go to the bank today.

questions.def: 'Ought to' is similar to 'should', used for advice.
questions.question: He ___ to help his mother.

questions.def: 'Necessity' is the noun form.
questions.question: There is no ___ to buy a new car.

questions.def: 'Mustn't' expresses strong prohibition.
questions.question: You ___ touch that. It's dangerous!

questions.def: 'Should' is used for recommendations.
questions.question: I ___ visit my grandma this weekend.

questions.def: Use 'doesn't' with 'he'.
questions.question: He don't have to work tomorrow. It's Sunday.

questions.def: 'Required' is the past participle, used with 'are'.
questions.question: You are ___ to show your ID.

questions.def: Use 'has to' for 'she, he, it'.
questions.question: She ___ to wear glasses to read.

questions.def: 'Mustn't' expresses strong prohibition.
questions.question: We ___ be late for the train.

questions.def: Use the base form after 'advise that'.
questions.question: I advise that he ___ to the doctor.

questions.def: 'Needs to' expresses necessity.
questions.question: He ___ to study harder if he wants to pass.

questions.def: 'Don't have to' expresses lack of obligation.
questions.question: You ___ apologize. It wasn't your fault.

questions.def: 'Recommend' is the base form, used to give advice.
questions.question: I ___ you to see this film.

questions.def: 'Should' is used to give advice.
questions.question: They ___ wear helmets when cycling.

questions.def: 'Doesn't have to' expresses lack of obligation.
questions.question: He ___ to go to the party if he doesn't want to.

questions.def: 'Obligation' is the noun form.
questions.question: There is no ___ to attend the meeting.

questions.def: 'Shouldn't' is used to give negative advice.
questions.question: You ___ drive so fast in the city.

questions.def: 'Has to' expresses obligation.
questions.question: She ___ call him. He's waiting for her.

questions.def: 'Should' gives advice. 'Must' is a stronger obligation.
questions.question: You ___ to wear a helmet when cycling.

questions.def: 'Have to' expresses external obligation. 'Must' implies personal.
questions.question: I ___ go to the meeting, but I'm very busy.

questions.def: 'Must' is followed by the base form of the verb directly.
questions.question: You must to call your mother today.

questions.def: 'Advise' is the verb form for giving advice.
questions.question: I ___ you to see a doctor.

questions.def: 'Shouldn't' gives advice against doing something.
questions.question: You ___ eat so much sugar; it's bad for you.
